title: Public source counts are not nested sets, so J3's counting funnel cannot reconcile them: web/evidence.json's 219 source ids = 215 live registry sources + 3 unregistered ids (okc_council_statement, okc-contract-c241032, osm) + gated deflock; 3 live sources (fbi_cde_agency_registry, osm_element_history, primegov) are absent from it; 12 live sources have no run row; 2 run-row sources (ccops_sf, okc_procurement) recorded 0 claims; 1 live source (state_alpr_statute_inventory) is not ingestion_permitted
evidence: GET web/freshness.json (sha256 c5a34382…): 178 source ids; GET web/evidence.json (sha256 3df209d5…): 255 artifacts, 219 distinct source; home and /evidence/ text 'Independent sources 218' = len({source_id} over publishable tier-0 weight rows) (exports/src/exports/analytics.py:590); gcloud storage ls -l -r ops/runs/** 21:34:25Z: 387 objects, 7,023,338 B, 208 source prefixes; tomllib sources.toml: 342 rows, 236 ingestion_permitted=true; PD/data/source_coverage.csv: 218 ingested-live. Set arithmetic: freshness ⊂ evidence (178 of 178); evidence − registry = {okc_council_statement, okc-contract-c241032, osm}; evidence − ingested-live = those 3 + deflock (gated, no rights block); ingested-live − evidence = {fbi_cde_agency_registry, osm_element_history, primegov}; run-row − ingested-live = {ccops_sf, okc_procurement}; ingested-live − run-row = 12 sources; ingested-live − permitted = {state_alpr_statute_inventory} (one-time seed, permitted=false by design). J3 §4.1 defines a nested funnel registered ⊇ permitted ⊇ scheduled ⊇ ingested ⊇ published_claims ⊇ published_sites; with these overlaps adjacent 'differences' are not id lists of a step. Fix: one universe (registry rows), one lifecycle partition, named attributes (K9 §3).

title: Freshness volatility 'unknown' on all 178 rows is a code conflation, not a data gap: volatility votes are cast only over dated observations, yet every predicate the freshness page reads has a registry volatility class (camera_latitude/longitude/name SLOW 2y, camera_jurisdiction GLACIAL 10y); only staleness needs dated observations (refines F-133 and J3 G-4, which route the whole fix to PKG-10 as a data-model question)
evidence: source_freshness_rows (shaping.py:1305-1336) skips claims with observed_at None ('continue') before predicate_meta() is consulted, and sets volatility 'unknown' when no dated registry observation exists; SHAPING_PREDICATES = (camera_latitude, camera_longitude, camera_jurisdiction, camera_name) (shaping.py:98-107); predicate_registry.json: 184 predicates, camera_latitude/longitude/name volatility_class SLOW half_life 2y, camera_jurisdiction GLACIAL 10y; live page 21:34:42Z 'Volatility classes: 178 unknown'. Volatility is a property of the predicate, so the dominant class and distribution are computable from all of a source's claims today; staleness (stale_count) legitimately needs dates and should show 'not evaluable: n undated' (F-133). Fix: K9 §5.2 (UX9-2).

title: Raw capture digests are not an upstream-change signal: at least 5 sources changed every capture digest within 0.1-8.8 h with identical claim counts (e.g. camreg_achd_id 25 min apart), and 12 consecutive run pairs kept identical digests while emitted claims rose 7-12% (SIG-side change, e.g. camreg_baltimore_md 6,888 -> 7,749); J3 NEW-3's fix ('last capture whose digest differs') would mislabel both, and only Eyes on Flock reads an upstream-declared last-updated field (refines F-369)
evidence: I1's local copy of all 387 run rows (docs/build/logs/next-phase/I1/runs_concat.txt; digests only, no bytes read): per source, consecutive outcome=ok rows with capture_digests: 157 pairs; 106 identical digest sets; 13 pairs with changed digests but identical claims_added, of which single/few-target disjoint cases camreg_achd_id (0.4 h), camreg_raleigh_nc (0.3 h), procportal_nyc_ny (0.1 h), uk_surveillance_camera_commissioner (0.3 h), camreg_arlington_va (3 targets, 8.8 h); 12 pairs with identical digest sets but different claims_added (camreg_baltimore_md, glasgow_gb, lambeth_gb, nola_la, northayrshire_gb, ottawa_on, peel_on, rochester_ny, sheffield_gb, winnipeg_mb, york_gb, dot_511_mo; 2026-09-17/18 -> 09-27/30). Connectors: only flock_portal keys change on the upstream's data_last_updated (SIG-INGEST-030c); ArcGIS/Socrata paths read no lastEditDate/rowsUpdatedAt (grep). Inference: volatile response bytes (ordering, timestamps) cause false 'changed'; connector/extractor changes cause claim-side change with unchanged bytes. Fix: upstream-declared last-modified per target, else a canonical records digest at flush; a separate 'last change in SIG records' column (K9 §5.4).

title: Execution history cannot be keyed on ingest_run: 324 of 387 run rows (all started before 2026-09-24T23:49Z) carry no ingest_run_id, pre-P31.2 executions shared 20 reused ingest_run rows (so ingest_run.started_at and code_commit describe the shared run, not the execution), 23 rows remain unmatched by the P31.2 backfill, fetch_record.fetches exists on only 58 rows, and J3 §4.5 maps a run's 'started' to ingest_run.started_at
evidence: Key presence over I1's local copy of the 387 rows: ingest_run_id on 63 (first 2026-09-24T23:49:26Z), absent on 324 (09-16..09-23 + early 09-24); fetch_record.fetches/logical_run on 58; one live row read (gcloud storage cat camreg_achd_id/2026-09-19/2026-09-19T07-09-57+00-00.json, 21:36:06Z) has no ingest_run_id and no fetches key. P31.2 read-back: ingest_run 20 rows all 'running' ('Under the pre-P31.2 reuse-by-key'), backfill appended 301 completions from 324 rows, 23 unmatched (6 failed no-claims, 8 zero-claim/tenant sweeps, 7 connector first run later, 2 overlapping retries). scheduled.py:559-562 records code_commit (SIG_CODE_COMMIT, rolled image digest) on the run only when set; runner.py:506 default 'unknown'. J3 §4.5 table: 'started / finished / duration | ingest_run.started_at, ingest_run_completion.finished_at'. Consequence: a naive run log shows the first execution's start and code for every later execution on a shared run and silently drops the 23 unmatched executions. Fix: execution-keyed history with link_basis/clock_basis (K10 §9, UX10-2).
